WoW: Forever

WoW: Forever class guides

Nine class guides for World of Warcraft: Forever, written from Blizzard's own notes and the beta client rather than from rumour — and honest about the large amount nobody knows yet.

WarriorRage is normalized to weapon speed and crits no longer feed it. Devastate does not exist.PaladinProtection finally has a taunt — and it costs you a rotational button.HunterMisdirection is gone, pets inherit your stats, and Survival is genuinely melee.RogueEnergy regenerates continuously, poisons crit, and Mutilate locks out Adrenaline Rush by one point.PriestDiscipline became a real spec. Most of what is written about Priest is demo-build data.ShamanAlliance Shaman exist. Windfury was rebuilt. The tanking ban has no Blizzard source.MageArcane Blast, Hot Streak and Fingers of Frost are new. Molten Armor is not in the game.WarlockDamage curses became Banes, so you hold one of each. The debuff cap is unanswered.DruidSkyborne can be Druids. Bear lost its threat talent and has no route to crit immunity.

How to read these

Forever launches 4 November 2026 and its first raids do not open until 9 December, five weeks later. Blizzard is running no raid PTR, the later dungeons and raids are encrypted, and item stats are obfuscated until an item drops for you or someone on your realm. The beta runs to 21 October and its level cap is still 20 — a rise to 30 was announced but never dated. So every class guide in existence, including these, is a level-20 guide. Any site showing you a level-60 best-in-slot list or a tank tier list for Forever has invented it. We would rather tell you that than fill the gap. Where something is confirmed, we say so plainly. Where two sources disagree, we say which and why. Where Blizzard has simply never answered — and there is a lot of that — we say it is unanswered instead of guessing.

The changes that touch every class

  • Hit is one stat. Melee, ranged and spell hit are merged, and so is crit. From the client's own combat-ratings table: 10 rating per 1% hit, 14 per 1% crit, 10 per 1% haste and expertise, and Defense converts at 1 because it is still a skill.
  • Talent trees kept their vanilla shape but gained a 16-point milestone alongside the old 11, 21 and 31.
  • There is no DoT or HoT snapshotting. Stats update dynamically, which kills every vanilla snapshotting habit. Periodic damage can crit.
  • Weapon skill still works but items carry far less of it, and no weapon-skill racials remain — they all became crit.
  • Expertise is new, and vanishingly rare: exactly one item in a 2,797-item catalogue carries it.
  • Haste exists but no gear has it. The only sources are racials and one PTR-flagged enchant.

Three specs tank: Protection Warrior, Protection Paladin and Feral Druid in bear form. Shaman is widely said to be ruled out — and that claim has no Blizzard source, which the Shaman guide goes into.

A word on sources

The beta has had exactly one balance pass, on 24 September. Every build since reads "talents, spells and items did not change". That makes this data unusually stable and also barely tuned — a launch-day pass could invalidate a good deal of it. Re-read before you commit to a main.
